name: cd-to-pptx
what_it_does: Turns a slide deck exported as a web page into a real PowerPoint file you can edit, leaving charts and diagrams as labelled empty boxes for you to fill in.
what_you_get: A `.pptx` file saved as a new version, a list of the placeholder boxes to fill by hand, and a note of anything that did not come across cleanly.
on_your_computer: Reads your deck folder, builds a new PowerPoint file and some check images there, and installs missing conversion tools from the internet if they are not already on the machine.

name: chart-discipline
what_it_does: Decides which chart fits the question, cuts the colors back to one that matters, and makes the chart say its point in a sentence rather than naming its axes.
what_you_say: what chart should I use for this? or "clean up this graph"
what_you_get: Chart rules applied to your slide, and a score out of 100 with a sorted list of what to fix if you run its checker.
on_your_computer: It runs two small local programs that read a chart description you point at and print advice; nothing is written, installed or sent anywhere.

name: deck-scaffolding-builder
what_it_does: Plans a deck before any slide is made: a slide-by-slide outline, a design spec, a layout map, an optional rough wireframe, and a build plan.
what_you_say: plan out a deck on our Q4 results
what_you_get: A set of planning documents in your deck folder, with clear markers where your own knowledge is still needed.
on_your_computer: It writes a set of planning documents for your deck into the folder you name, and searches the web only if you say yes when it offers.

name: html-diagram
what_it_does: Builds one interactive web page that diagrams a system: boxes you can click for detail, and buttons that light up a single path through the diagram.
what_you_say: make an architecture diagram of this system
what_you_get: One HTML file you open in a browser, two screenshots of it, and a note of the judgment calls made about the architecture.
on_your_computer: It writes an HTML diagram and two screenshot images into your working folder, can download and install a headless browser to take those screenshots, and the diagram it makes calls out to Google for a font whenever someone opens it.

name: layout-critique
what_it_does: Asks whether a slide reads: whether the eye lands in the right place, whether there are too many type sizes, whether the slide is too busy.
what_you_say: does this slide read, or is it too busy?
what_you_get: A pass or fail against each layout question, with the fix attached to each failure.

name: sales-lens-review
what_it_does: Asks whether a sales slide or sheet would really help someone sell: whether it starts a conversation or only answers one.
what_you_say: would a sales leader actually use this?
what_you_get: Direct notes on what a seller could and could not do with the asset, and what to change.
